text: {"repairs":[{"path":"analysis_steps[1].validation.evidence[0]","found":true,"loc":"Purity and completeness","quote":"We quantify the *fidelity* level of our sample based on the number of negative peaks in our 1-mm cube, using the same line search procedure."},{"path":"analysis_steps[2].fitting.evidence[0]","found":true,"loc":"Blind [CII] line candidates","quote":"For each spectrum we fit a single Gaussian to the candidate line emission, thereby deriving an integrated intensity ($I_{\\rm [CII]}$) and line full width at half maximum (FWHM)."},{"path":"analysis_steps[2].validation.evidence[0]","found":true,"loc":"Other redshift possibilities","quote":"We have thus used two important sources of information to reject other redshift possibilities and assess the reality of our \\[CII\\] line candidates, as described below."},{"path":"analysis_steps[3].fitting.evidence[0]","found":true,"loc":"Photometric redshifts","quote":"computed based using the best-fit chi-square at a given redshift derived from the full set of *HST* optical and NIR photometry for a source using the `EAZY` photometric redshift code"},{"path":"analysis_steps[4].validation.evidence[0]","found":true,"loc":"Continuum emission: Individual sources and stack","quote":"Assuming lower dust temperatures in our calculations, $T_{\\rm d}=25$ K, yield FIR luminosity and SFR$_{\\rm IR}$ estimates a factor $(2.5-3.0)$ lower."}]}
